environmentFirst: Use case: stylized-concept. Production game sprite atlas for Project Ember: bright simplified chunky PIXEL ART ancient frost ruins. Create exactly 3 columns x 3 rows on a square 1536x1536 transparent canvas, nine equal 512x512 cells, generous empty gutters, no cell border or text. Each object fully inside its own cell, 3/4 isometric view, calm limited 24-color palette, ivory pale blue stone, slate blue shadow, sparse cyan ice and dark sage foliage. Large deliberate pixel clusters and hard stepped edges, no blur or soft shading. Row1: tall narrow broken frost stone pillar with broad ice cap; low rubble of three angular blue stone slabs; low frost fern shrub in three broad icy leaf fans. Row2: low snow-covered broadleaf ground foliage; three faceted ice crystals of different heights; broken pointed mirror arch with transparent opening and two blue stone pillars, distinct silhouette from round courtyard arch. Row3: frozen cascade between two short pillars, only three broad angular ice ribbons; quiet rhombus isometric blue stone paving slab low contrast; rhombus paving crest with simple silver three-pronged snowflake inset, no letters. Each object centered horizontally with foot near lower fifth of its cell. No characters, no ground shadows, no glow, no background, no grid, no writing. Genuine alpha transparency including arch opening; no checkerboard image. Assets must be visually unique frost architecture, not recolored warm vines.
